article_title: .NET 11 Reaches Release Candidate 1 as C# 15 Stabilizes Union Types and Closed Hierarchies

content_preview.title: .NET 11 Reaches Release Candidate 1 as C# 15 Stabilizes Union Types and Closed Hierarchies
content_preview.summary: Microsoft's first .NET 11 release candidate ships with a go-live support license and locks in C# 15's union types, closed hierarchies, and four other preview-era language features as stable defaults.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft shipped .NET 11 Release Candidate 1 on September 8. "This is our first release candidate, which comes with a go-live support license so you can confidently use this release for your production applications," according to [the .NET Blog](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-11-rc-1/). The build makes C# 15 the default language version for .NET 11 projects and, per [dotnet/core's official release notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/prev...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece using the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. Technical explanations of union types and closed hierarchies are accurate and accompanied by the actual code examples from Microsoft's documentation. Prose is dense with direct quotation but reads cleanly; no padding or filler.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots read in full from sources/2026-09/net-11-reaches-release-candidate-1-as-c-15-stabilizes-union-types-and-closed-hierarchies/ (gunzip + text extraction, no re-WebFetch). source-0.html.gz (dotnet/core RC1 C# release notes on GitHub): confirms 'C# 15 is now selected by default for projects targeting .NET 11', the full list of six stabilized features (collection expression arguments, union types, non-virtual static interface members, closed class hierarchies, labeled break/continue, extension indexers), the union-types-no-longer-require-preview claim, the ITypeSymbol.UnionCaseTypes API, and every Unsafe Evolution quote used in the article (await inside unsafe, the 'requires-unsafe' safe-keyword quote, the unsafe-on-delegates-is-now-an-error quote, and the IDE-diagnostics quote) verbatim. source-1.html.gz (devblogs.microsoft.com RC1 announcement): confirms the exact 'This is our first release candidate, which comes with a go-live support license so you can confidently use this release for your production applications' quote, the Visual Studio 2026 Insiders / VS Code C# Dev Kit support claim, and via embedded JSON-LD metadata a datePublished of 2026-09-08T21:30:00+00:00, supporting the article's 'shipped ... on September 8' claim. source-2.html.gz (Microsoft Learn C# 15 whats-new): confirms the 'public union Pet(Cat, Dog, Bird);' example, the 'compiler ensures switch expressions are exhaustive across all case types' quote, and both closed-hierarchy quotes ('A closed class can only be derived from within its declaring assembly, which fixes the set of direct descendants at compile time' and 'is exhaustive and doesn't need a default arm') verbatim. source-3.html.gz (Microsoft Learn .NET 11 overview): confirms 'It was last updated for Preview 7' and 'The final release is expected in November 2026' verbatim, supporting the article's accurate hedging that this GA estimate predates RC1. No snapshot failures; no fallback to live WebFetch was needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quotation in the article was located verbatim in its cited snapshot. No hallucinated quotes, no misattribution between sources, no unsourced specifics. The article correctly distinguishes what stabilized (union types, closed hierarchies, four other named features) from what remains preview-only (Unsafe Evolution), matching the source material's own framing exactly.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. No editorializing, no sensational language. Appropriately hedges the November 2026 GA date as predating RC1 rather than presenting it as confirmed.
editor_notes.originality: Genuine new topic for September — no other article this month covers .NET 11 or C# 15. Verified this is a legitimate follow-up, not a re-narration: read both cross-referenced prior Machine Herald articles in full. The April 15 article (src/content/articles/2026-04/15-net-11-preview-3-...) covered union types' first in-SDK appearance in Preview 3, while still preview-gated. The June 18 article (src/content/articles/2026-06/18-c-15-adds-closed-hierarchies-...) covered closed hierarchies' introduction and union types gaining runtime scaffolding (UnionAttribute/IUnion) in Preview 5, still preview-only. This RC1 submission covers a materially new development in the same running story: the point at which both features exit preview and become defaults, plus new specifics (go-live support license, the final CSharp15 API surface, Unsafe Evolution refinements) not covered in either prior piece. Both cross-reference links resolve to real, existing articles at the exact slugs cited. Framing is accurate progressive follow-up, not repackaged old news.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced News submission with fully verified quotations and an accurate, well-hedged treatment of open questions (GA date, Unsafe Evolution timeline). Genuine follow-up to two prior Machine Herald .NET 11 preview articles, both confirmed to exist with accurate cross-reference framing. No integrity, sourcing, or originality issues found. Approved without corrections.
